en: The Scripture on the Great Compassion Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Minister Dharma Xian, Grand Master of Enlightened Teaching, Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
and Recipient of the Title of Chao San Da Fu, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, there was a sea deity named Mahāprema.
Having approached the place where the Buddha was, and having arrived there,
he prostrated with his head at the ground to pay homage to the Buddha’s feet,
then withdrew to stand to one side and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, I have a vow to benefit sentient beings;
may the Buddha, out of compassion, grant me permission to proclaim it.
At that time, the World-Honored One knew that this great heart of love would bring great benefit.
And he addressed her, saying: "Excellent, excellent!
For your benefit, speak as you wish.
At that time, Mahāprajāpatī, having received the Buddha’s permission, [proceeded].
He then addressed the Buddha, saying,
"I and my retinue dwell upon the great ocean,
where we frequently see sentient beings fallen into the perils of the sea."
Out of compassion for these beings, I wish to proclaim this dhāraṇī so that they may not be harmed by the perils of the sea.
World-Honored One, if there are sons or daughters of good family, or even bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās...
Those who hear this dhāraṇī, read, recite, and uphold it,
as well as those who hear the names of myself and my retinue,
shall all be completely liberated from every peril within the great ocean.
At that time, Mahāmaitrī, empowered by the Buddha’s majestic authority, spoke this dhāraṇī:

Tadyathā: julu julu | tulaṃdare | mahābhaṅgasiddhe | kuniṣka niṣke | anāhu | caṃpare | julu julu | samantavajre | akṣi cakri | cakradaraṃ | purāṇi svāhā || Then, Mahāmaitrī, the goddess of the ocean, received the Buddha’s holy command.
Having spoken this dhāraṇī,
they rejoiced with great exultation, prostrated before the Buddha, and withdrew.
This concludes the *Buddha-bhāṣita-mahāmaitrī-dhāraṇī-sūtra*.
